report.say:
The run came back empty. researchPrime loaded and then stopped at its own greeting — "✓ researchPrime loaded — what would you like to do?" — and idled there. It never entered the external scan. No brief, no sources, no adopt/adapt/ignore tags, nothing written to disk.

The cause is visible in the transcript, and it's one we've seen: the commission brief arrived mangled. Whitespace was collapsed into run-together text — "Beginthe commissioned work now", "Otherwiseworkon;wheneveryougenuinelyneedJohn'sdecision" — and the brief fragments landed out of order, with the tail about COVID replacement examples appearing above the COMMISSION BRIEF header. A skill that can't parse its own brief falls back to the idle greeting, which is exactly what happened.

That's the same write-path defect journal 0080 recorded and marked RESOLVED with paced ConPTY writes at Anchor 4d152d4. So either the pacing fix doesn't cover the commission path, or it regressed. Worth confirming which before spending another run — a re-fire onto the same broken path buys nothing.

The step itself is untouched. External scan is still open: how others run AI-conducted oral exams, AI-integrated statistics courses, and candidate running examples to replace COVID. Downstream, assessment-policy-decisions, homework-model-sets and block-1 authoring are all still waiting on it.
report.recommend: Verify the paced-write fix covers the commission-brief path, then re-fire the external scan — don't re-fire blind.

reflection.impact: No campaign content moved — the change is that the commission machinery itself is now proven broken again. The brief-mangling defect journal 0080 marked RESOLVED at Anchor 4d152d4 reproduced on the commission path: researchPrime received run-together, out-of-order text and idled at its greeting. This is the third run whose value the delivery lane lost (two Gandalf verdicts written but never handed back, now a mangled brief), so that lane — not any engine — is the campaign's critical path. Every step queued behind the external scan (assessment-policy-decisions, homework-model-sets, block-1-quiz-1) stays blocked until the commission write path is verified fixed; re-firing onto it as-is buys nothing. John's re-costing question from the prior run also remains unanswered.

next.directive: External scan for the BA 815 revamp, grounded in what is now known: 13 sessions with only 2 distinct post-intro lecture decks, so roughly 9-10 sessions will be authored fresh — the running example must sustain a full authoring arc, not decorate existing slides. Find and tag adopt/adapt/ignore: (1) how others run AI-conducted oral exams — conduct, rubric and transcript practice, integrity, accommodation and appeal paths, with the NYU Stern material on file as the known prior; (2) AI-integrated MBA or intro statistics courses — what they grade when an agent can do the mechanics; (3) candidate running examples to replace COVID carrying categorical and continuous variables through the full GLM arc (regression, logistic, ANOVA, dummy-variable) and workable in R, Python, and Excel. Answers feed assessment-policy-decisions, homework-model-sets, and block-1 authoring.
next.why: Three downstream steps queue behind this scan, and the authoring-scale finding makes the running-example choice a foundation decision — chosen late, it forces rework across ~10 freshly authored decks. The directive is fully determined; only the delivery path blocks it.
next.needs_human_why: The commission write path must be confirmed fixed before this launches: John needs to establish whether the Anchor 4d152d4 pacing fix never covered the commission lane or has regressed (an expert-coder job in his terminal), since a re-fire onto the broken path wastes the run exactly as this one was wasted.

oranges: The delivery lane has now silently eaten three runs' value (two unhanded Gandalf verdicts, one mangled brief) — until a regression test covers the commission write path specifically, every 'quiet' outcome should be treated as suspect and checked against disk before re-firing.

Journal 0080 marked the mangling RESOLVED but verification evidently covered only the interactive path — a fix without a commission-lane regression test invites a third recurrence at a more expensive moment, e.g. mid-Foreman build.

The roadmap is still priced as deck editing while the evidence says ~10 of 13 sessions are authored from scratch; every day that re-costing decision waits, the block-rebuild steps and any future Crucible plan inherit a scope that is roughly wrong by a factor of three.
